body:
**PM note (`domain:services` seat) — considered for dispatch this round and deliberately NOT dispatched yet. Card stays `pm:queue`, unassigned, no severity re-rated.**

This is the highest-value card in the seat's queue right now — p1, security, reachable on `main`, remedy already prescribed and proven by PR #15948. It is held only on a sequencing collision, and I am recording the collision so the next seat to reach it does not walk into it.

## The collision, measured

One of the four sites is **`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts:976`**. That file is currently owned by an open PR:

```
git diff --name-only 1375344b616743b73f85152961974e1f8a5f9069 bc0872bf0caba66bd6ae119d62c5d11316ddb2a2
  .changeset/approvals-continue-restored-suspension.md
  content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx
  content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx
  docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md
  packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts     ← the collision
  packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts
  packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/restored-approval-continuation.test.ts
  scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json
```

That is **PR #15966** (card #15389), currently in **round 3** of contract review — round 2 returned DOES NOT PASS, so it is not near landing.

`No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is a required check in this repo. A PR opened for this card today would take `approval-service.ts` while #15966 holds it, and that check would red — not as a nuisance, but correctly: two PRs editing the same authorization-adjacent file in parallel is exactly what it exists to prevent.

## Why not just split the card

Because the card forbids the outcome that splitting would produce, and it is right to:

> ⛔ Do not let a lane boundary leave one of the four unfixed while the other three land — a single remaining name-read reopens the hole.

Splitting **by lane** (the `runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts` note) is the split the card sanctions. Splitting **to dodge a live PR** is not — it would land three fixes and leave the fourth name-read live behind a green PR, which reads as closed while the hole stands.

## Unlock condition — ⛔ measure the tree, never a PR's own state

```
git fetch origin main   # unpiped
git log origin/main --oneline | grep -c '(#15966)'      # expect 1
git grep -n "positions" origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts
```

⚠️ The second command is the *routing* check, not the fix check — ⛔ do not read a hit or a miss there as evidence about this card's four sites. #15948's instance was written through the constant `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_PLATFORM_ADMIN`, so a string search for the literal name returned **zero on both the broken and the fixed head**; the card already says so under *What the taker owes*, item 2. Drive the sites.

Once #15966 is on `main`, this card is takeable as one PR across all four sites with no carve-out.

⚠️ One thing this note does **not** claim: that the hole is any less live for being held. It is reachable on `main` today, and #15972 (the write-side card that would make these readers harmless rather than merely correct) is also still open. If a seat can take this without touching `approval-service.ts`'s current head — or if #15966 closes rather than lands — that changes the calculus, and I would rather be corrected than have this sit.

## Hold condition, re-measured on the tree (not on any PR's own state)

```
git fetch origin main
git log origin/main --oneline | grep -c '(#15966)'   -> 1
git log origin/main --oneline | grep -c '(#15235)'   -> 1
git log origin/main --oneline | grep -c '(#15948)'   -> 1
origin/main head: b3820c3e2
```

All three are on `main`. The sequencing hold recorded in the PM note above is lifted, and the carve-out it was worried about is not needed: this is takeable as **one PR across all four sites**.

## Single-writer check — CLEAN, and measured rather than trusted

Enumerated all **34** open PRs, fetched each head ref locally, and diffed each against its own merge-base with `origin/main` restricted to the four files. **Zero** open PRs claim any of them.

Positive control, so the clean result is a measurement and not a silent no-op: the same scan against PR #16035 returns `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-provenance.ts` — it sees that package and reports hits there. #16035 touches `sharing-rule-provenance.ts` and **not** `sharing-rule-service.ts`, exactly as dispatch said.

Separately, `scripts/check-single-claim-paths.mjs`'s declared `SINGLE_CLAIM_PATHS` list holds exactly one entry, `.objectui-sha`, which this PR will not write.

## Sites re-located on current head

The card's line numbers predate the #15235 / #15966 landings, so all four were re-located rather than carried over:

| file | card | current head |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts` | `:254` | `:329-330` |
| `plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` | `:976` | `:1095`, `:1106` |
| `runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts` | `:149` | `:148-149` |
| `plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts` | `:117` | `:113`, `:117` |

Next: drive each of the four per the card's item 1 — per site, not inferred from the shape — before changing anything.

Owed to @os-zhuang's landing hold (5556942832), which has been open since 04:39Z. The verdict above it (5556932887) is **PASS** and needs no re-read — head `a8d29e2a` has not moved.

**The gap was mine.** `pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:525-536` makes the claim comment step 2 of the PM's atomic pair, first line the literal `Claim:`, carrying a mandatory `Clause-②:`. The existing claim (5555995683) opens `**Claimed by the os-dev seat.**`, which `/^\s*>?\s*Claim(?:ed)?\s*:/mi` cannot read — `**` is not whitespace. I verified that reading against the shipped parser rather than by eye; the full root-cause note is on #16097 (5557652999).

**The declaration is my own reading.** ⛔ Not a transcription of the verdict — a declaration I merely copied would not be one. The four sites stop deriving platform-operator authority from a NAME in `ExecutionContext.positions` (which any tenant can mint) and read the ADR-0095 posture rung instead. Nothing is added to or removed from a published surface.

⚠️ Stating the one place a reader could reasonably push back, rather than leaving it implicit: this change **does** move an accept/reject boundary — that is the whole point of the fix. My reading is that clause ② asks about a *contract's* accept set (what the platform will parse, accept or expose), and what narrows here is an internal authorization predicate whose pre-fix breadth was itself the security defect. On ADR-0095's own terms the rung was always the authority; the name check was never a contract anyone was owed. So: conformance repair ⇒ `no`. The director measured the same answer independently across four `.d.ts` files, which is concurrence rather than my source — and if this reasoning is judged wrong, the correction is a `yes` plus `needs:contract-review` on both carriers, not a quiet re-file.

<sub>`domain:services` PM seat · claim carrier corrected at the documented spelling; p1 `security`</sub>
